title: Open banking compared: Pakistan draft, UK, Brazil, India
sourceKey: Source ids match the numbered source list for Part 3

PK.value: SBP draft regulation; all banks, MFBs and EMIs must expose APIs
PK.note: Draft for consultation; not yet in force

UK.value: CMA Retail Banking Market Investigation Order 2017; nine largest banks (CMA9) created and funded the implementation entity, Open Banking Limited
UK.note: Moving to a not for profit future entity without statutory enforcement powers (S10, pp. 7 and 19 to 20)

BR.value: Banco Central do Brasil; mandatory data sharing participants; new governance structure defined by the central bank

IN.value: RBI licenses Account Aggregators as NBFCs; banks acting as financial information providers must share on a valid consent artefact
IN.note: The directions do not say every bank must join (S14)

PK.value: Central API hub on Raast run by RPP; bilateral or multilateral links also allowed for account information

UK.value: Standards body with directory and certification services
UK.note: Whether traffic routes through a hub: NOT FOUND

BR.value: Standardised system for sharing among participating institutions

IN.value: Several licensed aggregators pass data from providers to users and may not hold it

PK.value: Explicit, specific, time bound; scope, duration, purpose, payment limits; NADRA biometric check, bank OTP, app PIN; online dashboard; revoke any time
PK.note: No maximum duration; no non app path

UK.note: The consent rule (regulation 67 of the Payment Services Regulations 2017) was not read for this comparison

BR.value: Customer authorises sharing to receive offers; Pix Automatico authorisation can be cancelled any time with a maximum amount, tracked in the bank app

IN.value: Consent artefact records identity, data type, purpose, recipients, creation and expiry dates; revocable in whole or part

dimensions.label: Liability for unauthorised payments and recourse

PK.value: Bank credits customer within 7 business days of a valid claim, unless it suspects customer negligence, and recovers from provider if at fault; burden of proof on firms; RPP resolves bank and provider disputes
PK.note: Burden of proof rule closely follows UK regulation 75 (S19)

UK.value: Account provider refunds by end of next business day; payment initiation provider compensates it if liable; provider must prove authentication, and recorded PIN use is not enough on its own

BR.value: NOT FOUND for open finance; for Pix, Special Refund Mechanism applies in scam or fraud
BR.note: Pix rule, not an open finance rule

IN.value: No standalone liability clause; complaints resolved within one month, then RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme
IN.note: Account Aggregators share data only; no payment initiation

PK.value: No live service; three firms (Neem, Digi Khata, Swich Retail) in the sandbox cohort selected January 2026, up to six months

UK.value: 16.56 million connected users and 32.93 million payments in November 2025; over 40 million payments in May 2026; 1 billion cumulative by June 2026

BR.value: 96 million accounts connected; over 154 million active consents; over BRL 15 billion in payments in 2025

IN.value: 352.19 million accounts linked; 595.11 million consents fulfilled (cumulative)
IN.note: As on 30 September 2026; accounts and consents, not people
